narration.text: Pavement markings warn, regulate and inform drivers and carry the same legal force as traffic signs or signals. Yellow pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions, while white markings separate traffic moving in the same direction. Dashed markings are permissive, solid white markings are restrictive and solid yellow markings prohibit the indicated movement. Driving on the roadway shoulder is prohibited, according to the marking guidance. Preferential lanes for buses or carpools are identified by diamond markings and special signs. Compare each requirement separately before combining it with another. Preserve who the statement covers, the action it describes and any exception it states.

lines.text: A divided or one-way roadway has a yellow line at its left edge.
Retain the complete statement.

narration.text: A divided or one-way roadway has a yellow line at its left edge. A shared center lane reserved for two-way left turns is for left-turning vehicles from either direction, rather than through driving, acceleration or passing. A reversible center lane changes its permitted direction during specified periods and requires signs or signals. Dashed yellow markings on a two-way, two-lane roadway indicate where passing is permitted. Solid yellow centerlines prohibit passing but do not prohibit turning across them into a driveway. A single solid yellow edge line identifies the left side of a divided roadway. Compare each requirement separately before combining it with another. Preserve who the statement covers, the action it describes and any exception it states.

lines.text: Dashed white lines separate same-direction lanes where changing lanes is not restricted and lane use
is unspecified.

narration.text: Dashed white lines separate same-direction lanes where changing lanes is not restricted and lane use is unspecified. Solid white lines can mark special-use lane boundaries where lane changes are discouraged. Solid white lines may mark the pavement's outside edge or the shoulder edge; remain in the lane until moving out is safe. A pavement arrow reserves its lane for the indicated movement, which drivers in that lane must make. Pavement words warning of a school, railroad crossing or stop ahead require extra caution and preparation to stop. White transverse markings identify stop lines, crosswalks and parking spaces. Compare each requirement separately before combining it with another. Preserve who the statement covers, the action it describes and any exception it states.

Do not pass on either side of a vehicle stopped at a crosswalk for a pedestrian. Compare each requirement separately before combining it with another. Preserve who the statement covers, the action it describes and any exception it states.

narration.text: If a vehicle is stuck on the tracks and warning lights begin flashing, immediately get everyone out. After leaving a vehicle trapped on the tracks, run away from the vehicle and tracks toward the direction from which the train is approaching, then call nine-one-one once clear. The handbook warns that a train may reach a crossing only twenty seconds after warning lights activate, so do not delay escape. If a vehicle is stuck on tracks before warnings activate or where no warning lights exist, get out and immediately call nine-one-one and the crossing's emergency-notification number.
